# ddr_ctrl: generation prompt

*Generated by `ip/scripts/make_ip_prompts.py` from the RTL and testbench sources on 2026-10-25. It follows `ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md`; edit any field before use.*

```text
Create a new SystemVerilog IP block for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library.
```

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `ddr_ctrl_top` (IP directory `ddr_ctrl`)
- Library category: `memory`
- Location: `ip/memory/ddr_ctrl/`
- One-line purpose: Generic DDR controller: NPORTS AXI4 slave ports in front of a DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem's: one command per clock, read data T_CL clocks after RD).
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: standalone library block.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate):

| Module | From | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axil_if` | `shared/src` | AXI4-Lite interface of the FPGA Cores 4 U library, the common definition every block's register-bus ports follow. |
| `regbus_if` | `shared/src` | Simple register bus between an AXI4-Lite front end (axi4_lite_slave, axil_regbus) and the register block: one-clock write / read strobes, error answers that become SLVERR. |
| `axi4_lite_slave` | `axi4_lite_slave` | Generic AXI4-Lite slave front end. |
| `fallthrough_fifo` | `fallthrough_fifo` | First-word-fall-through FIFO with valid/ready handshakes. |

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`, `s_axi_awburst`, `s_axi_arburst`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil** - interface `axil_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`), ADDR_W = 8.
- **s_axi_*** - AXI4 (full) slave, address [NPORTS*ADDR_W-1:0], data [NPORTS*DATA_W-1:0]: discrete ports (bursts and IDs; the library has no full-AXI4 interface).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Declare bus ports as interface ports (`axis_if.slave s_axis`) with the interface, modport and parameters in a comment line directly above: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Widths are module parameters (Icarus has no $bits of an interface member); connect `.p(inst)`, not `.p(inst.mp)`. Yosys reads a top with interface ports through its discrete wrapper (`ip/scripts/syn_wrap.py`, sv2v); cocotb tests drive such a wrapper's plain ports.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clk` | input | 1 | - | - | clock |
| `rst_n` | input | 1 | - | - | synchronous, active low |
| `dfi_cmd_o` | output | [2:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | 0 NOP 1 ACT 2 RD 3 WR 4 PRE 5 PREA 6 REF |
| `dfi_bank_o` | output | [BANK_W-1:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | - |
| `dfi_row_o` | output | [ROW_W-1:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | - |
| `dfi_col_o` | output | [COL_W-1:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | - |
| `dfi_wrdata_o` | output | [DATA_W-1:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | - |
| `dfi_wrstrb_o` | output | [DATA_W/8-1:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | - |
| `dfi_rddata_valid_i` | input | 1 | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | the memory's read word (T_CL after RD) |
| `dfi_rddata_i` | input | [DATA_W-1:0] | DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem) | - | - |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Generic DDR controller: NPORTS AXI4 slave ports in front of a
DFI-style command interface (ddr_mem's: one command per clock, read data
T_CL clocks after RD). Version 1.0.0. Golden model:
model/ddr_ctrl_model.py (clock exact; tb/python, with ddr_mem).
- AXI4: full-width transfers (AxSIZE = log2(DATA_W/8)), INCR bursts of up
  to 256 beats, IDs passed through, the low address bits below a word
  ignored, WLAST not checked (AxLEN counts the beats). Another size or
  burst type answers SLVERR, a burst reaching beyond the memory
  (2**(BANK_W+ROW_W+COL_W) words) DECERR; an error burst touches no memory
  (reads return 0, writes take their W beats).
- Address map: word w = addr >> log2(DATA_W/8); col = w[COL_W-1:0], bank
  the next BANK_W bits, row the next ROW_W bits (row-bank-column).
- One burst at a time, beats in order. Each clock, in this order: (1) a
  refresh owed: PREA once every open bank is past T_RAS / T_WR / T_RTP,
  REF once every bank is closed and past T_RP (both T_RFC after a REF),
  nothing else; (2) a burst: an error beat per clock (read with credit,
  write with WVALID), or for the beat's bank / row (not within T_RFC of a
  REF): a hit past T_RCD issues RD (past T_WTR, with read credit) or WR
  (WVALID: WREADY, write data to the memory), another open row PRE (past
  T_RAS / T_WR / T_RTP), a closed bank ACT (past T_RP, T_RRD); (3) no
  burst: the arbiter grants a request (ARREADY / AWREADY combinational on
  the valid; index 2*port + write; a write only with room in its B FIFO;
  PRIORITY 1 lowest index, 0 round robin after the last grant); the
  burst starts the next clock.
- Refresh: every T_REFI clocks one more REF is owed (at most 15), each REF
  takes one: on average one REF per T_REFI however late each is served.
- Reads: every read beat enters a T_CL-deep return pipe alongside the
  memory and, at its end, its port's read FIFO (fallthrough_fifo,
  RQ_DEPTH) with the memory word (0 for an error), ID, RRESP, RLAST; a read
  beat needs credit (beats issued, not yet taken by RREADY) < RQ_DEPTH.
  Writes: the last beat pushes {BID, BRESP} into the port's B FIFO.
- Statistics (32-bit, wrapping, the regs port's sts_*): read beats, write beats, ACTs, row
  hits (memory beats issued without an ACT for that beat), REFs, error
  bursts; CTRL[0] written with 1 clears them (an event in that clock is
  not counted). STATUS: [0] a burst active, [4:1] refreshes owed.
Register map: src/include/ddr_ctrl_regs.json (ddr_ctrl_top.sv joins it,
  ID "DDRC", to the regs port, ddr_ctrl_regs_if).
The bank state and timing ages are ddr_mem's (saturating at 255), so the
controller keeps every timing rule.
Parameters: NPORTS (1 ..), DATA_W, ADDR_W, ID_W, BANK_W, ROW_W, COL_W, the
timings in clocks (1 .. 254; T_REFI >= 2), PRIORITY, RQ_DEPTH, BQ_DEPTH
(powers of two, 2 .. 64).
Clock - clk (AXI and DFI). Reset - synchronous active low rst_n.
Clock-domain crossings - none. Latency - a read beat T_CL + 1 clocks from
RD to RVALID; a burst starts the clock after its grant.

ddr_ctrl with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the block
designs and testbenches instantiate: the register map ddr_ctrl_regs
(u_regs, src/include/ddr_ctrl_regs.sv, ID "DDRC", VERSION and DATE at
0x00-0x08, the registers from 0x10) and the logic ddr_ctrl (u_core,
src/ddr_ctrl.sv), joined by the register interface ddr_ctrl_regs_if
(u_regs_if). Generated by ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py from
ddr_ctrl_regs.json and the ports of ddr_ctrl: regenerate after changing
either. Clock - clk. Reset - synchronous active low rst_n.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - ddr_ctrl (2026-10-25)
// Sources:
//   [1] Arm, "AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification" (IHI 0022, issue H), https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ihi0022
//   - A3.3.1 channel handshake dependencies (a slave may wait for AWVALID / AWREADY before WREADY,
//   for ARVALID / ARREADY before RVALID; a master must not wait for READY before VALID), A3.4 burst
//   types, sizes and lengths (INCR up to 256 beats, no 4 KB crossing: the master's rule), A3.4.4
//   responses (SLVERR, DECERR), A5 transaction IDs (one ID per read burst returned in order is legal)
//   [2] JEDEC, "DDR4 SDRAM Standard", JESD79-4 - timing tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tRTP, tWR, tWTR, tRRD, tRFC,
//   tREFI; refresh postponement (up to 8 REFs postponed, 9 x tREFI between two REFs)
//   [3] B. Jacob, S. Ng, D. Wang, "Memory Systems: Cache, DRAM, Disk" (Morgan Kaufmann, 2008), ch. 13
//   - open-page policy, row-bank-column address mapping, refresh priority over requests
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   Open-page controller: a request to the open row of its bank issues RD / WR at once (row hit),
//   to another row PRE then ACT (row miss), to a closed bank ACT; each command waits for its JEDEC
//   timings; refresh preempts requests once owed (PREA, then REF with every bank closed); every
//   tREFI one REF is due, on average one per tREFI.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: AXI4 handshakes (AWREADY / ARREADY on grant, WREADY during the burst after the
//   address - [1] A3.3.1 permits it), INCR full-width bursts, SLVERR / DECERR, in-order responses per
//   port; the open-page policy with row-bank-column mapping; every JEDEC timing rule listed (checked
//   independently by ddr_mem); refresh first with PREA / REF and the owed count, so REFs are not
//   postponed beyond the PREA timings (at most T_RAS / T_WR / T_RTP + T_RP clocks, far below the 8 x
//   tREFI postponement that [2] allows; the 15 cap is never reached for T_REFI > 2 x 254 + T_RFC).
//   Simplifications (deliberate, a generic controller for the library's frame stores and the NPU):
//   one burst at a time in grant order (no command reordering, no bank parallelism across bursts, as
//   in simple FPGA soft controllers); WLAST not checked (AxLEN counts the beats); the 4 KB rule left
//   to the masters; no narrow (AxSIZE < bus width) or WRAP / FIXED bursts (answered SLVERR); no ECC,
//   no tFAW, no self-refresh / power-down, no mode-register or ZQ sequencing (the PHY's job).
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```

### Register map (from `ddr_ctrl_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "DDRC" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x10 | CTRL | WO | 0 | [0] write 1: clear the statistics | - |
| 0x14 | STATUS | RO | 0 | [0] a burst active, [4:1] refreshes owed | - |
| 0x18 | RD_BEATS | RO | 0 | memory read beats (RD commands) | - |
| 0x1C | WR_BEATS | RO | 0 | memory write beats (WR commands) | - |
| 0x20 | ACTS | RO | 0 | ACT commands (row openings) | - |
| 0x24 | HITS | RO | 0 | memory beats issued without an ACT for the beat (row hits) | - |
| 0x28 | REFS | RO | 0 | REF commands | - |
| 0x2C | ERRS | RO | 0 | error bursts (SLVERR: size or burst type, DECERR: beyond the memory) | - |

The block is generated, not hand-written: write the JSON above and run `python3 ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py ip/memory/ddr_ctrl/src/include/ddr_ctrl_regs.json`, which also emits the C header and Markdown documentation. Extend the generator rather than editing its output.


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 1588 LUTs, 849 flip-flops. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking directed testbench for ddr_ctrl_top in front
of ddr_mem (2 ports, 64-bit words, 4 banks x 16 rows x 8 columns,
T_REFI 200). Checks, independently of the Python model (a byte-array
shadow memory in the testbench): bursts written on both ports read back
with their IDs, RLAST and OKAY, with random gaps on W and back-pressure
on R and B; concurrent traffic from both ports; partial write strobes;
SLVERR (wrong size, FIXED burst) and DECERR (beyond the memory) with
read data 0 and the memory untouched; refreshes kept on schedule; the
statistics counters and their clear; ID / VERSION and SLVERR on a
read-only write; and that ddr_mem never reports a timing violation
(every DDR timing rule kept). +define+MUTATE corrupts one shadow byte:
the testbench must then fail (mutation check). Test tasks in
tests/ddr_ctrl_tests.sv. Prints TEST PASSED on success.
```

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh ddr_ctrl --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_register_map` | ID, VERSION, idle STATUS, SLVERR on a write to a read-only register |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_write_read` | Bursts of 1 .. 16 beats on each port, across columns, banks and rows, read back |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_both_ports` | Both ports write and read their own data at once (same bank, other rows: PRE / ACT between the bursts) |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_strobes` | Partial WSTRB writes keep the other bytes |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_errors` | SLVERR (size, FIXED burst) and DECERR (beyond the memory): read data 0, memory untouched |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_refresh` | About one REF per T_REFI while idle |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_statistics` | RD / WR beats, ACTs, HITS, REFS, ERRS against the DFI commands; CTRL[0] clears them |
| `ddr_ctrl_tb` | `test_timing_kept` | ddr_mem reported no timing violation |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C memory/ddr_ctrl test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
